These three regions can be expressed as linear combinations of three indicator matrices (one for each rectangular block), so the resulting matrix has rank at most 3 for any grid resolution. I therefore expect the maximal rank to be 3.

4.text:
The flag of Tonga consists of a solid red field, a white rectangle in the upper-left canton, and a red cross inside that canton. Consequently, every row of the pixel matrix belongs to one of at most four combinatorial types:

- non-canton rows (all entries equal to \(a\));
- canton rows that intersect neither arm of the cross (leftmost block of entries equal to \(b\), remainder equal to \(a\));
- canton rows that intersect only the vertical arm (a single contiguous sub-block inside the canton set to \(a\), remainder of the canton set to \(b\), and the field outside the canton set to \(a\));
- canton rows that intersect the horizontal arm (a contiguous horizontal slab inside the canton set to \(a\), remainder of the canton set to \(b\), and the field outside the canton set to \(a\)).

Hence the matrix admits at most four distinct row vectors and its rank is at most 4.  

Any matrix of the indicated form may also be written
\[
M=bJ+cR,
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(R\) is the 0-1 indicator of the red pixels. The support of \(R\) consists of a full rectangle minus a smaller rectangular region that itself contains a cross; this geometry forces \(\operatorname{rank}(R)\le2\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)\le1+2=3.
\]
The bound 3 is attained for generic choices \(a\neq b\) (equivalently, generic scalars \(b,c\)), because the three summands that generate the column space remain linearly independent.

Thus the maximal possible rank is exactly 3.
